1.explanation:
These six files are where the affected components declare and document their accessibility props in Storybook and in the official component docs. 

• Modal/Modal.mdx & its overview: defines the kebab-case aria-label prop for the Modal header, matching the first screenshot. 

• ComboBox/ComboBox.mdx & its overview: shows the camelCase ariaLabel prop for the listbox, matching the second screenshot. 

• OverflowMenu/OverflowMenu.mdx: one of the other key components in the task list that currently uses ariaLabel. 

• CodeSnippet/CodeSnippet.mdx: another component in the plan-of-action checklist with a documented ariaLabel prop. 

Reviewing these files will let you see exactly how each component’s props are defined, how Storybook surfaces them, and where to apply the refactor to support consistent aria-label usage across the library.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots reveal an inconsistency in how WAI-ARIA props are exposed across Carbon React components. In the Modal story (first image), the Controls panel lists the accessibility prop as “aria-label” (kebab-case) for the modal header. However, in the ComboBox story (second image), the same kind of accessibility label is exposed as “ariaLabel” (camelCase). Behind the scenes several other components (e.g. OverflowMenu, CodeSnippet, NumberInput, etc.) also differ in whether they accept only aria-label, only ariaLabel, or both. This inconsistency leads to confusing documentation and prop handling, and must be unified so that every component supports the hyphenated aria-label prop in JSX as per React’s accessibility guidelines.
